comment: The module's own entry point, which Ghidra already calls `entry`; the hand-written restatement names it as "the module entry" and names no symbol for it, so this row carries the address and the comment and leaves the name alone. It dispatches through the library constructors at 0x3EC into OemOcDxeMain (0x4F8).

The "library constructors" of the hand-written restatement: the static-init chain that resolves gRT and gST before the module body runs. The restatement names them in prose and gives them no symbol, so again the row carries the address only.

name: OemOcDxeMain
comment: What this module decides on every boot: (1) EC 0x0741 bit 7 set -> overclocking recovery: turn CpuSetup's "OverClocking Feature" off, raise UniWillVariable.OverClockRecoveryFlag, clear the EC bit. (2) otherwise -> copy UniWillVariable.MemoryOverClockSwitch into Setup[0x7D7], which is the byte that un-suppresses the "Memory" (Memory Overclocking Menu) link on the vendor Advanced page; if the switch is 1 and OC is enabled, drive PCH pad GPP_B22's TX state high; and copy the Control Center's CPU core-voltage values into CpuSetup. EC_0741_OC_RECOVERY is BIT7 of that byte; bit 0 of the same byte is "AP exist". Reached from the module entry at 0x3D0 through the library constructors at 0x3EC. The byte is seeded from the low byte of ImageHandle and only overwritten if the EC read succeeds, so a failed read tests an uninitialised value (as decompiled; not observed).

name: MemOcGpio
comment: Runs only when MemoryOverClockSwitch == 1, and only if CpuSetup.OverclockingSupport == 1. The tables at RVA 0x1550 (17 entries) and 0x1750 (15 entries) are Intel's GPIO_GROUP_INFO for CNL/CML-H and -LP PCHs (0x1E bytes each: PID, PadOwn, HostOwn, GpiIs, GpiIe, GpiGpeSts, GpiGpeEn, SmiSts, SmiEn, NmiSts, NmiEn, PadCfgLock, PadCfgLockTx, PadCfgOffset, PadPerGroup). The H/LP choice (0x1100) is the 00:1F.0 device ID: 0x068x/0xA30x -> H, 0x028x/0x9D8x -> LP. Group 1 of the H table is PID 0x6E, PadCfg 0x790, 26 pads: GPP_B. PCR MMIO is 0xFD000000 | PID << 16 | offset (SBREG_BAR); the TX-lock change goes through the P2SB sideband registers at 00:1F.1 (0x1270) with opcode 0x13, the value Intel's reference code names GpioLockUnlock. Nothing in this module drives the pad low when the switch is 0. What GPP_B22 is wired to on this board is not known from the BIOS; a DIMM voltage select would fit the "memory overclock" name, and is only that: a guess, untested.

name: OcRecovery
comment: The overclocking-recovery path, taken when the caller read EC 0x0741 bit 7 (EC_0741_OC_RECOVERY) set. Gets CpuSetup (0x2BB bytes, gCpuSetupGuid b08f97ff-...) and UniWillVariable (0xB4 bytes, UniWillVariable 9f33f85c-...), writes 1 to Uwv+0x5C (OverClockRecoveryFlag; GCUService shows a notice and clears it) and 0 to CpuSetup+0x1B7 ("OverClocking Feature"), and sets both variables back. Clearing the EC bit is the caller's job, immediately after this returns. The two offsets are read off the decompiler's stack layout of the two GetVariable buffers, not from a struct definition the module carries.

name: SyncOcVariables
comment: The menu gate. Setup[0x7D7] is question 0xEC6 in the IFR; the vendor Advanced form 0x2712 shows Ref "Memory" -> form 0x27B1 "Memory Overclocking Menu" only when 0xEC6 == 1 and CpuSetup[0x1B7] != 0, so Setup.Oem7D7 = UniWillVariable.MemoryOverClockSwitch (+0x33) is what un-suppresses the menu link. If the switch is 1, MemOcGpio (0x5D8) runs. If UniWillVariable.ApExistFlag (+0x5D) is 1, the Control Center's CPU core-voltage values are copied into the Intel OC knobs: ICpuCoreVoltageOffsetRangeType (+0x66) selects case 0 -> prefix 0 and ICpuCoreVoltageOffsetValue (+0x3A) -> CpuSetup+0x1BD; case 1 -> prefix 1 and ICpuCoreVoltageOffsetNegativeValue (+0x64) -> CpuSetup+0x1BD; case 2 -> the same as case 1 unless the negative value is 0, in which case as case 0. CoreVoltageOffsetPrefix is CpuSetup+0x1BF, and ICpuCoreVoltageValue (+0x34) goes to CpuSetup+0x1C0 "Core Voltage" in all three cases. Finally the ranges the service reads back as its slider limits are written: ICpuCoreVoltageMaximum = 2000, ICpuCoreVoltageMinimum = 0, ICpuCoreVoltageOffsetMaximum = 100, ICpuCoreVoltageOffsetMinimum = 0, as two 32-bit stores so the adjacent minimums become 0. evidence/uefi/2026-09-23-MemoryOverClockSwitch-set.txt shows 0x36 = 0x07D0 and 0x3C = 0x0064 in a variable this code wrote. CpuSetup is 0x2BB, UniWillVariable 0xB4, Setup 0x7D8 bytes.

name: PadOwnership
comment: Reads a PCH GPIO pad's ownership bits: returns 0 and EFI_NOT_FOUND unless 0x1158 accepts the PID, then takes bits 1:0 of the pad's PCR word at PadCfgOffset + 8, which for GPP_B22 is PCR[0x6E][0x38] bits 25:24. 0 is PadOwn HOST here, and the GPP_B22 caller (0x5D8) treats anything else as a reason to leave the pad alone.

name: SbiClearLockTx
signature: static EFI_STATUS SbiClearLockTx (UINT32 PidPort, UINT32 Pad, UINT32 Bits)
comment: Clears P2SB sideband lock bits, after the same PID check 0x1158 performs (a failed check returns EFI_NOT_FOUND without touching the sideband). 0x119C calls it with (0x301, 0, 0x400000) and the mask reaches the sideband helper as ~0x400000, i.e. bit 22, GPP_B22's TX-lock, is cleared so the pad register can be changed. 0x119C puts it back through SbiSetLockTx afterwards.

name: SbiSetLockTx
signature: static EFI_STATUS SbiSetLockTx (UINT32 PidPort, UINT32 Pad, UINT32 Bits)
comment: Sets the same P2SB sideband lock bits 0xD2C clears, with the same PID check. 0x119C calls it with (0x301, 0, 0x400000) to restore GPP_B22's TX-lock after the pad register has been written.

name: EcWritePortByte
signature: static EFI_STATUS EcWritePortByte (UINT8 Pair, UINT8 Value)
comment: Writes one byte to 0x66 (the EC command/status port) or to 0x64 (the KBC pair, selected by the port argument) after waiting for IBF=0. Part of the EC access sequence documented at 0xF38.

name: EcDrainObf
comment: Drains OBF: while the status port's bit 0 is set, reads the data port (0x62, or 0x60 for the KBC pair) and writes each byte to 0x80, then gives the EC 5000 units of time before re-reading. Part of the EC access sequence documented at 0xF38.

name: EcWaitIbfClear
comment: Waits for the status port's IBF (bit 1) to clear, with a short delay per poll, and returns EFI_TIMEOUT after 0x1FFFF polls. Part of the EC access sequence documented at 0xF38.

name: EcWriteCommandData
signature: static EFI_STATUS EcWriteCommandData (UINT8 Pair, UINT8 Command, UINT8 Data)
comment: EC access. ACPI EC ports: command/status 0x66, data 0x62 (the helpers take 'b' = 0x62; '`' = 0x60 would select the KBC pair 0x64/0x60). This one performs the whole write: wait for IBF=0 (0xED4), drain OBF (0xE4C), write the command byte to the command port (0xDD4), wait for IBF=0 again, optionally write the data byte to the data port, drain OBF again. Neither of the two sequences the hand-written reading calls EcRead0741 and EcWrite0741 is a single function: EcRead0741 is 0xA3 07, 0xA2 41, 0xA4, read 0x62, and EcWrite0741 is 0xA3 07, 0xA2 41, 0xA5 Data, and both are this function plus 0xDD4 and the data-port read. The vendor commands are 0xA3 <hi> and 0xA2 <lo> to set the EC RAM address, 0xA4 to read the byte at that address, and 0xA5 <val> to write it (all inferred). "Inferred" because the command semantics come from use, not from the EC side: OemUniWillVariableDxe (FUN_0000084c) uses the same 0xA3 07 / 0xA2 lo / 0xA4 sequence to fill UniWillVariable.ProjectID from lo = 0x40, i.e. EC 0x0740, which is the confirmed PROJECT_ID register (ec/annotations/registers.yaml).

name: IsPchLp
comment: Transcribed name, and it does not describe the return value: the decompile returns 1 when the 00:1F.0 device-ID class from 0x1100 is NOT -LP and the chosen table's PadPerGroup is > 22, and 0 otherwise. The name records the question being asked; the call site at 0x5D8 proceeds only on a non-zero return, which is what makes the early return in the hand-written reading of 0x5D8 ("if IsPchLp or PadPerGroup <= 22, return") come out right. Left as transcribed rather than renamed, with the discrepancy stated here rather than quietly fixed (CLAUDE.md). A device ID 0x1100 does not recognise becomes class 0xFF, takes the 17-entry H table, and so passes this check with PadPerGroup > 22: an unknown ID uses the H table.

name: MemOcSetGppB22Tx
signature: static VOID MemOcSetGppB22Tx (UINT16 Pid, UINT8 Pad, UINT64 Group, UINT32 TableSel)
comment: The routine the hand-written annotation labelled "/* 0x119C */" without naming; the name here is new. It is what 0x5D8 calls once the table and ownership checks have passed: read the pad's lock bits, if bit 22 (GPP_B22 TX-lock) is set clear it through SbiClearLockTx (0xD2C), then set PCR[0x6E][0x790 + 22*0x10] bit 0 (GPP_B22 DW0 GPIOTXState = 1) directly, then restore the lock through SbiSetLockTx (0xD80) if it had been set.
